The Philadelphia Phillies ’ need for right-handed offense is drawing attention early in free agency, with two established outfielders emerging as suggested additions to their lineup. Philadelphia finished last in OPS from right-handed hitters in 2026, according to MLB Network Radio. That ranking provides the backdrop for a discussion about strengthening the Phillies’ offense through the open market. The segment focused on players who finished the season with the Seattle Mariners and Chicago Cubs, respectively. Both now face qualifying-offer decisions that could determine whether they remain with those organizations for another year. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) MLB Network Radio shared host Mike Ferrin’s assessment Thursday on X, formerly Twitter, underscoring the connection between Philadelphia’s offensive shortcoming and available outfield talent. “Randy’s going to get paid, and he’s going to be a really good addition for somebody… The Phillies. top.title: Don’t buy this hype: Why Georgia is in danger against Ole Miss
top.description: Week 10 of the college football season brings us seven matchups between ranked teams, including a critical SEC clash of titans between Georgia and Ole Miss. Reigning SEC champion Georgia has more breathing room than two-loss Ole Miss, but both need this to go their way to further impress the College Football Playoff committee. Georgia comes into the game as a favorite, but Ole Miss could have one decisive advantage on its home field if they can exploit it. Make Gunner Stockton Win Through the Air Sep 27, 2025; Athens, Georgia, USA; Georgia Bulldogs quarterback Gunner Stockton (14) looks to pass against the Alabama Crimson Tide in the first half at Sanford Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Ole Miss enters Saturday’s matchup with a clear defensive objective: make Georgia quarterback Gunner Stockton uncomfortable and force the Bulldogs to rely on their passing attack. The biggest question about the Georgia offense remains its aerial offense. It struggled against one of the worst secondaries in the SEC a week ago. Florida ranked 112th nationally in EPA per pass and 126th in passing success rate. But the Bulldogs managed just 101 passing yards in an otherwise dominant win. Disrupt the Timing The Rebels need to challenge Georgia’s receivers at the line of scrimmage and disrupt Stockton’s timing. Physical coverage can delay routes developing and force him to hold the football longer, giving Ole Miss’ defensive front additional time to generate pressure. Defensive tackle Will Echoles could be especially important. His ability to collapse the pocket and disrupt throwing lanes could prevent Stockton from comfortably working through his progressions. More: Predicting SEC football scores for Week 10’s biggest games Take Away the Easy Throws Ole Miss should prioritize limiting Georgia’s short and intermediate passing options. Forcing Stockton into difficult third-down situations would give the Rebels opportunities to disguise coverages, bring pressure, and potentially create turnovers. The goal shouldn’t necessarily be to gamble for interceptions. Instead, Ole Miss must make Georgia earn every completion and avoid allowing yards after the catch. Turn Pressure Into Mistakes Georgia’s offense becomes less predictable when it stays ahead of the chains. If Ole Miss can stop the run on early downs, it can force Stockton into obvious passing situations. Ultimately, Ole Miss doesn’t need to completely shut down Georgia’s passing game. It needs to disrupt its rhythm, eliminate easy completions, and force Stockton to make difficult decisions under pressure. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

top.title: Why Chiefs WR Rashee Rice reportedly filed for bankruptcy after legal battles
top.description: Why Chiefs WR Rashee Rice reportedly filed for bankruptcy after legal battles originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy on Wednesday, court documents showed, per WFAA. Rice reportedly claimed over $3 million in debts in the filing, which came in the Northern District of Texas bankruptcy court. A majority of those listed debts, per ESPN , were tied to "varying plaintiffs suing him in civil litigation that have either been settled or are awaiting trial." Here's what's known about Rice filing for bankruptcy. MORE: NFL trade deadline predictions, projected landing spots Chiefs WR Rashee Rice files for bankruptcy According to WFAA, Rice filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy on Nov. 4, court documents showed, listing his estimated assets to be worth "between $500,000 and $1 million," and his estimated liabilities between "$1 million to $10 million." Rice listed various assets in the filing, including his Super Bowl 53 ring, a Mercedes-Benz, and NFL apparel, per WFAA. ESPN also reported that federal court records showed Rice claimed "more than $3.45 million in debts" in the filing, including more than $2.1 million of which is tied to civil lawsuits that have either been settled or are awaiting trial. The Chiefs wide receiver has been involved in multiple lawsuits tied to his role in a high-speed car crash in Dallas in 2024, along with an ex-girlfriend alleging he repeatedly assaulted her from 2023 to 2025, per ESPN . In July 2025, Rice pleaded guilty to two third-degree felonies in connection with the Dallas car crash incident. He served 30 days in a Dallas County jail in June 2026 after reportedly violating his probation terms after testing positive for THC. According to ESPN, in the bankruptcy filing, Rice claimed to have a total of $677,054 in personal assets, with his largest creditor owed $979,837 as part of a civil settlement related to the 2024 car crash. Rice is also still disputing potential debts from the civil lawsuits, including "a combined $700,000 in lawsuits filed by 2024 crash victims and $200,000 as part of the alleged assault suit," per ESPN. Rice's Super Bowl ring was also reportedly used as collateral with his attorney in the pending civil cases, valued at $160,000. Rice, 26, is in the final year of his rookie contract with Kansas City in 2026. According to Spotrac , he signed a four-year, $6.4 million deal with the Chiefs in 2023, set to hit free agency this upcoming offseason. Over five games this season, Rice has posted 20 catches for 243 yards and two touchdowns. MORE: Who needs Jonathan Taylor the most?

top.description: (Photo by Derick E. Hingle/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to Thursday’s NFL Transactions Report, the Kansas City Chiefs have added another receiver to their practice squad. Bub Means, a fifth-round pick of the New Orleans Saints in the 2024 NFL Draft, was listed as a practice-squad transaction for the Chiefs a day after he tried out for a spot. He was one of nine players Kansas City hosted for tryouts on Wednesday. The Chiefs also signed wide receiver Jacob De Jesus, who spent time with the team this offseason. top.title: ‘You want to be shaken and brought back to earth’: HC Mike Brown addresses Knicks poor start
top.description: Jun 5, 2026; San Antonio, Texas, USA; New York Knicks head coach Mike Brown speaks with the media after the game between the Spurs and the Knicks in game two of the 2026 NBA Finals at Frost Bank Center. Mandatory Credit: Daniel Dunn-Imagn Images The New York Knicks haven’t had the start to the season they expected, and the reigning champs may have celebrated too hard during the summer. But head coach Mike Brown isn’t worried about his team’s 3-4 start; rather, he’s “a little excited” about their current struggles. On Monday, the Knicks beat the Brooklyn Nets, defeating their neighbors across the bridge 103-90. The team has been off to a slow start, losing its first three games of the season and beginning its rivalry with the Philadelphia 76ers 0-2. The Nets looked competitive early, trailing just 51-44 at halftime, and they took a 79-75 lead into the fourth quarter after a 35-point third. But the defending champs rallied in the fourth quarter, as they are known to do, outscoring Brooklyn 28-11 to seal the deal. The next day, Brown was asked by a reporter, “Are you happy with the starts? Do you think the starts need to get better?” in reference to the team’s energy out of the gate. “Everything can get better,” Brown answered, via SNY Knicks on X . “Am I happy with it? I’m not pissed about the starts or upset about the starts. I’m actually — there’s a part of me… I’m a little excited that we’re struggling a little bit. Because I want to see if we, right now, can figure it out — not figure it out in 10 games and take off and win the last 72, cause that ain’t happening; we’re still going to go through our lulls. But when you go through the off-season that we just went through, where everybody celebrates you the way this lovely city did, and the fans of the New York Knicks did, you want to be shaken and brought back to earth right away when the season starts, because that grounds you; everybody, starting with me on down, obviously, is human, and sometimes you can get a little full of yourself. “So if you hit some challenges or some adversity early on, it helps you refocus a little bit quicker, which can help you get on track the right way sooner. top.title: Dodgers Have 2 Intriguing Trade Targets as Marlins Make Infielders Available
top.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers’ biggest position of need is second base if they want to upgrade offensively on what they have. Tommy Edman is one option at second, along with infield prospect Alex Freeland and possibly even Hyeseong Kim. If the Dodgers want another option, someone who had an impressive 2026 season or a better track record than either Kim or Freeland, the Miami Marlins have a pair of infielders who are reportedly available. Aug 16, 2026; Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; Miami Marlins shortstop Otto Lopez (6) high fives second baseman Xavier Edwards (9) after the victory over the Cincinnati Reds at Great American Ball Park. Mandatory Credit: Katie Stratman-Imagn Images Otto Lopez, shortstop, and Xavier Edwards, second baseman, are two players who, according to Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald , may be traded for “a lot” in exchange. Both Lopez and Edwards have three years of arbitration control, so they are under control until 2030. The Marlins don’t need either of them urgently, but it is an opportunity for at least the Dodgers to explore . Here is what the pair offers: Xavier Edwards Edwards is a multi-positional defender who can play second base and shortstop. His defense declined in 2026 after being above average. Still, he is a walking specialist, with an 11.4% walk rate; he avoids strikeouts (13.9%) and puts the ball in play, but doesn’t hit it hard. More importantly, he’s fast and ranks as an elite base-runner, with at least 21 SBs over the last three years. The Dodgers need speed, and Edwards’s .360 OBP means his speed shows up on the bases. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Dodgers Nation (@dodgersnation) Otto Lopez Lopez is likely the more expensive player, given how amazing his 2026 was. He put up a 5.9 fWAR season, with an above-average hitting season. Lopez slashed .305/.349/.437 with just 11 home runs, but drove in 94 runs, stole 34 bases, and drove in 71 runs. Sep 23, 2025; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Miami Marlins shortstop Xavier Edwards (9) and second base Otto Lopez (6) celebrate win against the Philadelphia Phillies at Citizens Bank Park. Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images It was far and away his best offensive year, since he struggled to get much going before. He is strictly a contact specialist who is a master at putting the ball in play, even if it means a weak walk rate of 5.8%. However, he also plays elite defense, with three straight years as one of the league’s best infielders. Lopez can slot in at either second base or shortstop, and he plays them at a high level. Who should the Dodgers target? Out of the pair, Edwards makes the most sense, since he is likely to cost a bit less and has a more stable track record. Lopez has only one year of hitting at the level he produced in 2026, and for what the Marlins may ask, he may need another season of similar production to warrant that many prospects.

nigeria.title: Bournemouth stay perfect in Europa League as Milan lose again
nigeria.description: Bournemouth extended their perfect Europa League record on Thursday as they came from behind to win 3-1 at 10-man Sparta Prague, while Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan suffered a third defeat in four matches. Gambian Ebrima Singhateh ran from his own half to score a fine individual goal as Sparta took the lead in the Czech Republic after Bournemouth midfielder Lewis Cook hit the post with a first-half penalty. Sparta had Tobias Guddal sent off before half-time and Bournemouth equalised through Tyler Adams on 57 minutes. Evanilson steered the Cherries ahead nine minutes from time and Rayan bagged a late third as Bournemouth’s substitutes sent the European newcomers top of the table with a fourth successive victory. Marco Rose’s side have won each of their past seven matches in all competitions ahead of a Premier League trip to Ipswich this weekend. “It’s a big achievement and we have to continue, we need to stay alert, sharp,” Rose told TNT Sports. “It’s up to us to use this momentum. Everyone tries to beat us, if we get in a comfort zone just a little bit we get in trouble.” Milan lost 2-0 at home to Ferencvaros as the Hungarians kept pace with Bournemouth, maintaining their 100 percent record in Europe. Haiti international Lenny Joseph struck twice in the second half at San Siro to earn Ferencvaros a deserved win over the seven-time European champions despite having Bamidele Yusuf sent off. “We gifted opportunities, made stupid errors. We were not prepared to play football tonight,” Amorim told Sky Sport. “I don’t want to lie to my players. We cannot play like this in front of our own fans. It was a very poor performance.” Milan are languishing outside the top 24 with just three points at the halfway stage of the league phase. “I won’t give up on this competition. As long as we’re not mathematically out of it, we’ll keep fighting,” Amorim added. Crystal Palace snatched a 1-1 draw at home to Hoffenheim as Japanese midfielder Daichi Kamada levelled in stoppage time. Alexander Prass gave Hoffenheim an early lead at Selhurst Park and Palace lost Adam Wharton to a second yellow card before Kamada rescued a point for Pierre Sage’s struggling side. Palace, last season’s UEFA Conference League winners, have five points from four outings in the Europa League but sit in the Premier League’s relegation zone, just behind Manchester United on goal difference. nigeria.description: A UK medic who tested positive for Ebola while working on the outbreak of the disease in the Democratic Republic of Congo has been flown to London for treatment, the government said Thursday. The unnamed British citizen “has returned to the UK for specialist treatment after testing positive for the disease”, the government said in a statement. Africa’s latest Ebola outbreak has killed more than 5,300 people, the vast majority of them in the Democratic Republic of Congo, according to the continent’s top health agency. The British government said that the UK medic is now being treated at the Royal Free Hospital in London. This hospital has a high-level isolation unit “specifically designed for this purpose” and strict protocols to prevent contact with the general public, it said. Renu Bindra, deputy director of the all hazards public health response team at the UK health security agency (UKHSA) said “the risk to the wider public remains low”. nigeria.title: 2027: Peter Obi Has Not Offered Any Alternative — Oshiomhole
nigeria.description: The Senator representing Edo North, Adams Oshiomhole, has said the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has not offered any alternative to the policies of President Bola Tinubu ahead of the 2027 general election. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, Oshiomhole described Obi as a trader whose approach, according to him, focuses on short-term gains rather than long-term national development. “Peter Obi has not offered any alternative. I think it is you or someone else who asked him for security, what will you do differently? He said, it’s in his heart. “I’ve always said that Peter Obi is a trader; the logic of a trader is short term turnover. A statesman that Tinubu represents thinks of the next generation,” he said. ﻿ Oshiomhole said he respected the right of opposition candidates to contest for the presidency but believed Tinubu should remain in office after “having gone through all the teething problems” rather than “recruit a new apprentice.” He also criticised the record of the administration of former President Olusegun Obasanjo, under which former Vice President Atiku Abubakar served, alleging that they were unable to guarantee the payment of workers’ salaries. The Edo North Senator said the 2027 presidential election would present Nigerians with a choice between Tinubu, whom he credited with unifying the exchange rate, and Atiku, whose administration he accused of allowing different exchange rates for people based on their connections. Oshiomhole also defended the Tinubu administration’s handling of workers’ welfare, saying the Federal Government’s approval of a ₦70,000 transport allowance showed that the President cared about them. “I think this government is doing well. If a man who was on ₦70,000 now is given ₦70,000 addition that makes it ₦140,000 for him it’s a hundred percent increase and if you know what ₦10,000 means for the real masses, you’ll appreciate that Tinubu has shown that he cares,” Oshiomhole said. The Federal Government approved the monthly ₦70,000 transport intervention for workers across all levels for six months, beginning in November 2026, following a meeting with the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) on October 27. The agreement also provides for the payment of outstanding peculiar allowances in three equal monthly instalments beginning in November. However, the Trade Union Congress (TUC) rejected the transport allowance, arguing that workers need a permanent salary increase rather than temporary relief. nigeria.title: ADC Court Ruling: ‘APC Afraid Of Strong Candidate Against Tinubu’ – Osunbor
nigeria.description: A former Governor of Edo State and National Legal Adviser of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Oserheimen Osunbor, has accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of being jittery ahead of the January 2027 presidential election. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, Osunbor said the APC did not want a strong candidate to challenge President Bola Tinubu at the polls. “I have said that repeatedly, they (APC) are afraid of any strong candidate running against President Bola Tinubu in the January presidential election,” Osunbor said. ﻿ The ADC legal adviser said the party and its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, were continuing with their campaigns because they believed the court judgment nullifying Atiku’s candidacy would not stand. “Our presidential candidate (Atiku Abubakar) and the presidential campaign is going on, unperturbed because we believe that this judgment will not stand and cannot stand,” he said. Osunbor said the party would appeal the judgment to ensure that a higher court sets it aside. He expressed optimism that Atiku would survive the current challenge, insisting that the former Vice President had the support of the people. “Atiku will survive because the people are behind him. The force of the people will be greater than the force of those who want to enslave Nigerians,” he said. Osunbor’s comments followed Thursday’s judgment by the Federal High Court in Abuja, which sacked the David Mark-led ADC leadership and invalidated actions taken by the party under the leadership, including the process that produced Atiku as its presidential candidate for the 2027 election. Justice Peter Lifu delivered the judgment in a suit filed by Nafiu Bala Gombe, a former National Deputy Chairman of the party, who challenged the process through which the Mark-led leadership assumed control of the ADC. nigeria.title: Traders attack Edo Consumer Protection Committee members over fake products
nigeria.description: By Ozioruva Aliu – BENIN CITY Member of the Edo State Consumer Protection Committee led by its chairman, Osaro Culture Iyamu were, on Thursday, attacked by some beverage sellers while trying to enforce ban on sales of fake, adulterated and unauthorised drinks along Mission Road in Benin City, the state capital. The committee members were on a routine mission to the area when they noticed that some sellers were removing cartons, bottles and cans of drinks from their shelves on seeing the committee members. The infuriated sellers then prevented the committee members from accessing their shops to ensure that what they had were genuine products. Consequently, security agencies have invited beverage sellers, including Beverages and Alcohol Dealers Association, for a meeting over the incident. Iyamu alleged that his committee had been under pressure to compromise. nigeria.title: Nigeria must deploy tollgates, technology to improve highway security – Musa
nigeria.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa (retd), has advocated restoring tollgates on major highways and deploying modern technology to enhance highway security and help identify and track criminals. Musa noted that tollgates could play a valuable security role, especially with modern technology that can identify and track vehicles without requiring drivers to stop for manual payments. The minister made the remarks at the Abuja roundtable, “Promise to Proof: The Renewed Hope Conversation,” organised by the APC Progressive Strategy Roundtable. It was convened by the Executive Chairman/CEO of PICNG and EVs, Ismaeel Ahmed. Responding to concerns about highway security and a suggestion that motorists could contribute through security levies at tollgates, Musa described the reintroduction of tollgates as a good idea, noting that Nigeria might have made a mistake by dismantling them. He explained that modern tolling systems in other countries use technology to identify vehicles through their registration numbers, with payments processed electronically, adding that such systems could also assist security agencies in identifying and tracking vehicles. The minister also called for the strengthening of Nigeria’s identification system through the use of personal identification numbers, facial recognition and fingerprints to improve security monitoring. He said technology would make it easier for security agencies to establish people’s identities and track criminal activities. On the broader security situation, Musa said the Federal Government was recording progress in tackling terrorism, banditry and kidnapping through increased defence investment, improved intelligence gathering, joint military operations and stronger cooperation among security agencies. He disclosed that the Federal Government allocated ₦5.4 trillion to defence in the 2026 budget and was recruiting an additional 12,000 military personnel to strengthen manpower and security coverage. According to him, the government was also investing in modern weapons, surveillance systems and operational platforms to improve intelligence gathering, mobility, firepower and rapid response capabilities. He further disclosed that Nigerian security forces killed more than 300 terrorists and bandits, including over 10 commanders, in operations conducted in the week preceding his presentation. The minister identified porous borders as a major challenge, noting that Nigeria shares extensive borders with neighbouring countries, particularly Niger Republic, through which criminal groups and illicit arms can move. He said the government was strengthening border security and expanding bilateral, regional and international defence cooperation through intelligence sharing, specialised training and technological support. Musa added that Nigeria continued to maintain security relationships with Niger, Burkina Faso and Mali despite their withdrawal from ECOWAS, including military training

nigeria.title: Italian chef sacked for refusing to put pineapple on pizza, says it insulted his culture
nigeria.description: An Italian chef in Australia has lost an unfair dismissal claim after being sacked for, among other workplace issues, refusing to serve ham and pineapple pizza, describing the topping as an insult to his culture. Davide Tamburella was dismissed from the now-closed La Costa restaurant in Brisbane in May, following a meeting with management over several complaints about his conduct. One of the issues raised was his refusal to prepare ham and pineapple pizzas for guests attending an event at the restaurant. According to a ruling by Australia’s Fair Work Commission, Tamburella argued that instructions from management “need not be followed when it is offensive to his culture”. The commission noted that the chef’s objection to the fruit was because “he considers, as an Italian, that putting pineapple on a pizza is an insult to his culture”. It also found that this was not the first time he had refused to use pineapple on pizzas, recording three such instances over four years. On a previous occasion, Tamburella had asked his employer to “check how important it is for Italians not to put pineapple on a pizza”. Beyond the dispute over pizza toppings, management raised concerns about his use of foul language, communication style and what it described as an “escalation of frustration in the workplace”. The ruling also detailed an incident in April when Tamburella fractured bones in his right hand after striking a metal handrail at work. The chef had reportedly hoped to secure employer sponsorship for a visa that would allow him to remain in Australia as a permanent resident. However, following his dismissal, the restaurant discontinued the sponsorship process. Tamburella subsequently approached the Fair Work Commission, challenging his dismissal. However, the commission rejected his unfair dismissal claim because it was lodged outside the permitted timeframe. The restaurant’s managing director, Elliot Ingram, told the Daily Mail there was “more to this story than a pizza topping”. The BBC said it had contacted Tamburella for comment. On his LinkedIn profile, the chef describes himself as someone whose career has focused on “delivering exceptional food” and “improving business performance”. He also shared a post titled “letter for chefs” three months ago, centred on the theme of “respecting the ingredients”. His LinkedIn profile indicates that he now works at another restaurant in Brisbane. A BBC check found that pineapple is not included on its menu. Meanwhile, Queensland, where the restaurant was located, is regarded as Australia’s pineapple heartland and produces the country’s commercially grown pineapples. The state is also home to the Big Pineapple, a 16-metre fibreglass structure on the Sunshine Coast that has become a popular local landmark. nigeria.title: 2027 UTME: JAMB moves to shut down substandard CBT centres
nigeria.description: By Joseph Erunke The Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) has moved to tighten its grip on the conduct of the 2027 Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME), warning that computer-based test (CBT) centres that fail to meet its prescribed standards will be denied accreditation. The Board said only centres with adequate facilities, reliable infrastructure and the operational capacity to guarantee a credible and hitch-free examination would be approved to host candidates in the 2027 exercise. JAMB Registrar, Prof. Segun Aina, gave the indication during a meeting with the leadership of the Chief External Examiners, where preparations and readiness for the accreditation exercise ahead of the 2027 UTME were reviewed. According to a post on the Board’s official X handle on Thursday, the meeting was part of efforts to strengthen examination administration and ensure strict compliance with established operational standards. The Board said the accreditation exercise would serve as a critical screening mechanism to prevent inadequately equipped centres from participating in the examination, thereby protecting candidates from avoidable disruptions and compromising examination conditions. Reiterating its position, JAMB declared that accreditation would not be automatic for CBT centres seeking to participate in the exercise. “Only centres that meet JAMB’s standards will be accredited to host the examination. For candidates, that means a fair and secure place to sit the UTME, wherever they write it,” the Board stated. The development signals JAMB’s determination to strengthen the credibility of the UTME by ensuring that candidates, irrespective of their examination locations, have access to a secure, reliable and conducive testing environment. The strict accreditation regime is also expected to address operational shortcomings that have historically threatened the smooth conduct of computer-based examinations, including inadequate facilities and poor technical readiness. With preparations for the 2027 UTME gathering momentum, the Board maintained that compliance with its accreditation requirements would remain non-negotiable for all CBT centres seeking approval to participate in the nationwide examination. nigeria.title: British woman, unborn baby die in Nigeria; family seeks help to bring bodies home
nigeria.description: A 40-year-old British woman who relocated to Nigeria to start a new life with her husband has died alongside her unborn baby after developing sepsis. Claire Chadwick, who was 37 weeks pregnant, reportedly suffered septic shock after her baby girl died in the womb. In a report by Daily Mail UK, Chadwick had moved to Nigeria to be with her husband, Ibrahim, and was expecting their first child together. She had built a social media following of thousands through videos documenting their relationship, religious beliefs and food challenges on TikTok and Instagram. Her death has left her family devastated, with her sister, Shannon, revealing that she is survived by her 19-year-old son in Wales, her husband and other relatives. Describing her late sister, Shannon said Claire was a funny and fiercely strong-minded woman who lived life on her own terms. “She was a woman who lived her life in her own way and she will leave a lasting impression on everyone who knew her,” she told WalesOnline. The family has since launched a GoFundMe campaign with a target of £10,000 to repatriate Claire and her unborn daughter to the United Kingdom for burial. Explaining the purpose of the fundraiser, Shannon said the family wanted to bring both bodies home so they could be laid to rest with dignity and surrounded by their loved ones. “More than anything, we want them both returned so they can be laid to rest with dignity, surrounded by the family who love them,” she said. The fundraiser has attracted widespread support, with Shannon describing the response as overwhelming. She also expressed gratitude to REST, a charity that supports families dealing with the sudden or tragic deaths of loved ones abroad. Tributes have also poured in from friends and well-wishers, who remembered Chadwick as a kind, caring and cheerful woman. One supporter recalled knowing her from childhood and described her as lovely, while another said she was devastated by the loss, remembering her as someone who always made people laugh. The family hopes to raise enough money to bring Claire and her unborn daughter back to the UK. nigeria.title: Zidane’s son dropped from Algeria squad for AFCON qualifiers
nigeria.description: Algeria goalkeeper Luca Zidane was left out of the national team squad on Thursday ahead of two Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers against Togo, coach Brahim Hemdani said. Zidane, 28, has recently been missing from the Algerian team, owing to injury and a two-game suspension over scuffles during an AFCON game against Nigeria in January. But his exclusion was “based on sporting criteria”, Hemdani told journalists. “I need to have three goalkeepers who were getting as much playing time as possible.” Hemdani called up USM Alger goalkeeper Oussama Benbot alongside Melvin Mastil of Swiss club Lausanne-Sport and Abdelatif Ramdane of MC Alger. Zidane, a son of French football icon Zinedine Zidane, joined the Fennecs after changing his sporting nationality in September 2025 to represent Algeria, where his family has roots. The Leganes goalkeeper’s absence came as a surprise, along with that of Manchester City defender Rayan Ait-Nouri. Ait-Nouri had been sent home in September following a reported dispute with the coaching staff during a match against Zambia. But Hemdani said there had been “no problem” after his choice not to include the left-back in his next 26-man squad, adding that there were “criteria for inclusion”. “However, anything is possible in the future, and no one has been permanently excluded,” the coach said. Algeria are set to face Togo on November 14 and 17. They have four points from two games and are currently top of AFCON qualification Group I, which includes Zambia and Burundi. nigeria.title: Nigerian teenager, Fawaz jailed four years for attempting to steal Porsche in London
nigeria.description: A 19-year-old Nigerian teenager, Fawaz Oyedeji, has been sentenced to four years in prison in the United Kingdom for attempting to steal a £72,500 Porsche Cayenne using an imitation firearm. Oyedeji, who is from Greenwich, London, posed as a prospective buyer after responding to an online advertisement for the luxury sports utility vehicle. He arranged to meet the seller at the victim’s home in Southwark on Tuesday, March 18, to inspect the vehicle. After the victim showed him around the Porsche, the pair entered the front seats to discuss the sale. Oyedeji then produced what appeared to be a firearm, pointed it at the seller and demanded the car keys. However, the victim resisted and fought back, forcing Oyedeji to abandon the attempt and flee from the scene. The police were subsequently alerted and launched an investigation into the incident. Detectives traced the phone used to arrange the vehicle inspection to Oyedeji, establishing that it had been in the vicinity of both his home address and the scene of the attempted robbery. Investigators also obtained CCTV footage showing his movements shortly before and after the incident. Clothing matching what the suspect wore during the attempted robbery was also recovered by officers. Oyedeji was arrested at his home on Leonard Robbins Path within 38 hours of the offence. A jury at the Inner London Crown Court found him guilty after just 26 minutes of deliberation on Wednesday, November 4. He was subsequently sentenced to four years’ imprisonment. Detective Constable Alex Long, who led the investigation, praised the victim for resisting the armed robbery and cooperating with investigators. “The victim showed immense courage by refusing to hand over his keys despite being threatened with what appeared to be a genuine firearm,” Long said. He added that CCTV footage, digital records and forensic evidence helped detectives build a strong case that secured Oyedeji’s conviction. The detective also urged people buying or selling vehicles privately to take necessary precautions, advising them to leave if a transaction appeared suspicious and call emergency services when necessary. nigeria.title: Bwala to David Mark-led exco: You took over ADC leadership undemocratically and hoped all is well

nigeria.description: By Olayinka Latona The wife of the General Overseer of the Redeemed Christian Church of God (RCCG), Pastor Foluke Adeboye, has called on parents, churches, governments and other stakeholders to take greater responsibility for raising children with godly character and values, saying Nigeria’s future depends on how its young people are nurtured. nigeria.title: Atiku Takes Presidential Campaign To Kebbi, Pledges To Restore Fuel Subsidy

business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Greece Approves 10% Crypto Capital Gains Tax as First Framework Lands Below Draft Rate Greece’s parliament approved on Thursday a bill that imposes a 10% capital gains tax on cryptocurrencies, the first comprehensive legal framework for taxing crypto assets in the country. Cryptocurrency capital gains of up to €500 ($563) a year will be exempt from the new tax, the bill says. For bitcoin holders in Greece, that threshold is a small buffer, not a carve-out for larger positions. “Further implementation directives will be published in the coming weeks, which will also define transparency and audit rules,” a senior finance ministry official told Reuters . An earlier draft circulated in October had floated a 15% rate. The version lawmakers passed lands five points lower, while keeping the €500 annual exemption that was already in that proposal. What the levy covers for bitcoin holders The tax is set to apply from Jan. 1, 2027, Greek coverage of the finance ministry bill says. It is levied on the net gain — the difference between the acquisition price and the transfer price — not on the full sale proceeds. Trading fees and other costs tied to the deal can factor into that calculation. A taxable transfer is not limited to selling for euros. Using cryptocurrency to buy goods or services, or contributing it to cover or increase company capital, can also crystallize a gain under the new rules. That matters for anyone in Greece who pays a merchant in bitcoin rather than converting first. Simply holding bitcoin while its euro value rises does not, by itself, create a tax bill. Crypto-to-crypto swaps, such as bitcoin for another token, are treated as non-taxable events in the explanatory material that accompanied the bill, matching the approach France has used to avoid taxing every hop between coins. Net annual gains at or below €500 are exempt. Purchases of crypto assets are also being pulled into Greece’s existing “source of funds” checks from 2027, so buyers may need to show that the euros used to acquire bitcoin or other tokens came from declared income or other lawful capital. The rule does not add a separate purchase tax; it widens the audit trail around how coins were funded. The update unlocks two new concepts: “Payjoin-by-default and Payjoin trading,” according to he press release shared with Bitcoin Magazine. Founded by Francis Pouliot in Canada in 2013, Bull Bitcoin is the world’s longest-running Bitcoin-only exchange. Its non-custodial platform lets customers in Canada, Europe, and Latin America buy Bitcoin directly into their own wallet and sell Bitcoin to their bank account. Bull Bitcoin also develops BULL Wallet , a free and open-source self-custodial Bitcoin wallet. The company has been self-funded since its inception. Payjoin is a Bitcoin onchain privacy protocol that breaks basic assumptions made by on-chain analysis firms about user behaviour. One such assumption is that one of the unspect transaction outputs (UTXOs) resulting from a bitcoin transaction will be change returning to the sender. Or that amounts are more often than not denominated in dollars. Payjoin protocols add an off-chain coordination layer such that the amounts sent and returned to the sender obfuscate user intent and thus protect their privacy on-chain. Payjoin does not require a hard fork or a soft fork into Bitcoin consensus. Instead, it must be adopted by user wallets and exchanges to scale, but it also does not depend on collective action to benefit individual users. Bull Bitcoin’s Payjoin integration is closely based on the Payjoin Foundation ‘s work. Every time a BULL Wallet user buys or sells Bitcoin on-chain via their built-in exchange, that transaction will be a Payjoin by default. This will allow Bitcoin buyers to passively aggregate their wallet’s UTXOs, which can reduce their Bitcoin mining fees in the future. “Many Bitcoin users do not even know that they must periodically “merge” their coins by spending them to a new address in their Bitcoin wallet, if they want to reduce the economic costs of future Bitcoin transactions,” explained the press release. Payjoin-by-default automates this process. The US$617 million programme is implemented by the Bank of Industry (BOI), which also co-finances it alongside the African Development Bank (AfDB), Agence Française de Développement (AFD) and the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB). It backs young Nigerians aged 15–35 and the businesses they build in the technology and creative sectors through skills development, enterprise support, access to finance and enabling infrastructure. CANEX WKND 2026 holds from 5 to 8 November 2026 in Lagos under the theme “One People, United in Culture, Creating for the World,” bringing together creatives, investors, financial institutions, policymakers and development partners from across Africa and the diaspora. At the heart of iDICE’s participation is the iDICE Deal Room, which will host structured meetings between 15–20 investment-ready creative and digital enterprises and investors and financiers, including iDICE-backed fund managers Ventures Platform and Kuramo Capital, the BOI-iDICE Debt Fund, the BOI Non-Interest Banking team managing the IsDB-supported facility, and participating financial institutions. The Deal Room aims to hold 40–50 investor–enterprise meetings and generate investment leads for follow-up after the event. iDICE and BOI will also take part in high-level sessions on financing and technology in the creative economy, and showcase programme-supported enterprises at the iDICE exhibition stand. “Nigeria’s digital and creative industries hold significant potential to drive economic growth, create jobs, expand exports and strengthen the country’s global competitiveness. Realising this potential requires sustained investment in enterprise development, access to finance and the capabilities of our young people. Through the iDICE Programme, the Federal Government and the Bank of Industry are working with development partners to address these needs and build a stronger ecosystem for digital and creative enterprises. CANEX WKND provides an important platform to deepen engagement with industry stakeholders, connect creative entrepreneurs to investment opportunities and advance the partnerships needed to grow the sector,”said Ife Adebayo . The National Coordinator of the iDICE Programme, Ife Adebayo, added: “The Deal Room is about turning conversations into investment. We are bringing some of the most promising enterprises from the iDICE pipeline to meet financiers ready to back them, while showing what iDICE is already delivering for young Nigerian founders and creatives.” Creative and tech entrepreneurs attending CANEX WKND 2026 are invited to visit the iDICE Exhibition stand to learn about available financing and support, including non-interest financing

entertainment.title: U.S. Consulate General Highlights Fashion’s Role in Expanding U.S.-Nigeria Commercial Ties During Lagos Fashion Week
entertainment.description: U.S. Consul General Brandon Hudspeth delivering remarks at the event hosted at the Consul General’s residence in Lagos. Consulate General Lagos recently recognized the contributions of Lagos Fashion Week founder Omoyemi Akerele at a lunch held at the height of Lagos Fashion Week 2026. The event recognized Akerele’s vision in connecting Nigerian designers with American consumers and creating new opportunities for U.S. businesses. The occasion brought together designers, entrepreneurs, and creative leaders to highlight fashion’s role in strengthening U.S.-Nigeria ties. “It’s an honor to celebrate Lagos Fashion Week 2026 with so many of Nigeria’s most talented designers and creative leaders. For 15 years, Omoyemi has built one of Africa’s premier fashion showcases, connecting Nigerian designers with American buyers and retailers and showing how trade creates opportunity for both our countries,” said U.S. Consul General Brandon Hudspeth . In attendance was also award-winning American-born actress and producer Osas Ighodaro . Guests also experienced a new fashion themed game developed by Lagos based Maliyo Games, highlighting fashion’s growing links with technology and entertainment. Lagos Fashion Week founder Omoyemi Akerele speaking at the event hosted by the U.S. Consul General in her honor, celebrating her vision in connecting Nigerian designers with American consumers and creating new opportunities for U.S. businesses. Fashion is a major global industry, supporting jobs and commercial activity across design, retail, and related sectors including in both the United States and Nigeria. U.S. consumers spent an estimated $560 billion on clothing and footwear in 2025, according to the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis. For Nigeria’s fashion industry, access to the American market offers a pathway to expand the reach of Nigerian designers while offering entry points into Africa for U.S. retailers and businesses. Since founding Lagos Fashion Week in 2011, Omoyemi Akerele has built the platform into one of Africa’s leading fashion showcases. Its 2025 edition featured more than 60 designers and welcomed approximately 15,000 guests. Lagos Fashion Week (LFW) has also become a bridge to the American fashion industry. Leading American singer Ciara walked the LFW runway in 2025, while Studio 189, the label co-founded by American actress Rosario Dawson , has shown collections in Lagos. New York-based Nigerian designer Tia Adeola has also featured her collections at LFW as well as American media outlets including Vogue and Essence being among the leading U.S. outlets that have covered the shows. LFW helps Nigerian designers explore the U.S. market through trade shows such as Coterie and NYNOW in New York and Liberty Fairs in Miami. entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought. Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. I was enjoying my holiday and had no reason to suspect my wallet was quietly making it more expensive than necessary. Then, one time, I was given change in a currency different from the familiar CUC. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. I did not recognise them, and I was not about to walk away with money I did not understand. So, I rejected the change. Imagine my surprise when the cashier and another customer explained to me that the notes were perfectly valid Cuban money! That was when I got my crash course in Cuban economics. entertainment.title: Ejiro Amos Tafiri Unveils REVERIE, Its Spring/Summer 2027 Collection, Celebrating Reinvention in African Luxury
entertainment.description: Ejiro Amos Tafiri , a Pan-African luxury fashion house founded in Lagos in 2010, has unveiled REVERIE, its Spring/Summer 2027 (SS27) collection, at an exclusive private showcase in Lagos on Sunday, October 25, 2026, held alongside Lagos Fashion Week. The showcase brought together distinguished guests, fashion industry leaders, patrons and representatives of the British Council Nigeria, including chef and media personality Hilda Baci, for a presentation of the house’s latest collection. REVERIE explores renewal and reinvention through contemporary African luxury. Bringing together expressive silhouettes, intricate craftsmanship and a refined colour palette, the collection presents a visual statement that celebrates the evolving language of African fashion. Through considered design and craftsmanship, REVERIE reflects the house’s continued exploration of contemporary African aesthetics, presenting pieces that balance creative expression with the distinctive design sensibility for which Ejiro Amos Tafiri is known. Founded by designer Ejiro Amos Tafiri, known for her signature Drapes, the fashion house has spent 16 years developing a distinctive identity within the luxury fashion landscape. Its design language is characterized by expressive drapery, fluid tailoring and the thoughtful use of indigenous textiles, bringing African craftsmanship into contemporary fashion. The Lagos unveiling followed the third edition of Fashioning a Legacy: Leaving a Mark in Time, held on Saturday, October 24, 2026, at the British Council in Ikoyi, Lagos. The conference brought together designers, stylists, retail professionals and emerging creatives to discuss building sustainable careers and creating lasting impact within the fashion industry. Together, the events reflect Ejiro Amos Tafiri’s continued engagement with the broader creative ecosystem, connecting fashion, education, craftsmanship and the development of emerging talent. The REVERIE presentation forms part of the house’s 16-year milestone and will be followed by an exclusive showcase in Abuja on November 21, 2026. The forthcoming event will bring together members of the diplomatic community, government officials, fashion patrons and invited guests for a further presentation of the house’s work. As Ejiro Amos Tafiri looks towards its next chapter, REVERIE embodies an ongoing exploration of renewal and reinvention, reinforcing the house’s commitment to advancing contemporary African luxury through expressive design and intricate craftsmanship. entertainment.title: Pan-African School Games 2026: Celebrating Young Talent, School Pride and New Opportunities
entertainment.description: The Pan-African School Games 2026 brought together young athletes from schools across Lagos for three days of swimming, athletics and football, celebrating sporting talent, school pride and the opportunities that organized competition can create for children and young people. Held at James Hope College, Lekki, from 16 to 18 October, the second edition of the Games featured the U-11, U-13 and U-15 categories. Students competed for individual honours and school points while gaining valuable experience in a structured, multi-sport environment. The competition also welcomed sporting stakeholders and scouts, reinforcing the wider ambition of the Pan-African School Games: to give young athletes a platform where their abilities can be demonstrated, recognized and developed. Building on the Inaugural Games The second edition of the Pan-African School Games built on the foundation established by the inaugural Games in 2025, continuing the vision of creating meaningful sporting opportunities for young athletes. The 2026 edition welcomed schools and student-athletes for three days of swimming, athletics and football, providing a platform for competition, talent development and school pride. Beyond the sporting results, the Games continued to advance a broader ambition: to connect schools, athletes, sporting stakeholders and educational institutions while creating opportunities for young people to develop their abilities and explore future pathways through sport. Day One: Swimming Opens the Games Swimming opened the competition, bringing young swimmers together for races across the U-11, U-13 and U-15 categories. The opening day set the pace for the Games as athletes took to the pool to test their abilities, pursue strong performances and earn points for their schools. The races highlighted the preparation, discipline and technique required to compete, while providing young swimmers with valuable experience in a formal sporting environment. For many of the students, the opportunity to compete alongside athletes from other schools added to the significance of the experience. Each race contributed to the overall competition, with schools beginning their campaigns for medals and category honours. Day Two: Athletics Puts Young Athletes to the Test Athletics took centre stage on the second day, with track and field events testing the speed, strength, coordination and technique of the young competitors. Athletes competed in running, jumping and throwing events, earning points for their schools as the standings developed. Each discipline presented a different challenge, giving students opportunities to demonstrate their abilities and compete for individual and team honours. The athletics programme added another dimension to the Games, highlighting the variety of talent within the participating schools and the value of giving young athletes opportunities to develop through competition. Under the overarching theme “One People, United in Culture, Creating for the World: From FESTAC ’77 to CANEX ’27,” this year’s gathering will connect thousands of creative entrepreneurs, investors, policymakers, and cultural icons from across Global Africa and the diaspora. Spotlighting Francophone Luxury & Made-in-Africa Fashion As part of this landmark event, Afrique Femme is hosting a dedicated Exhibition Pavilion designed to bridge Francophone and Anglophone creative ecosystems. The pavilion will feature curated showcases, pop-ups, and private sales from leading West and Central African designers. Attendees will experience exclusive collections from celebrated brands including Makeda by AYA Konan ,, KUMI , KWELAKU , and Galipette Atelier , highlighting the richness, craftsmanship, and global potential of Francophone fashion. The African Woman 2.0 VIP Networking Brunch A core highlight of the week will take place on Saturday, November 7, 2026 , with the African Woman 2.0 VIP Networking Brunch . entertainment.title: African Philanthropy Leaders Call for Bolder, Locally Led Giving at the 2026 APF Conference in Cape Town
entertainment.description: CAPE TOWN, South Africa: African Philanthropy Forum (APF) closed its 2026 Conference in Cape Town on 27 October with a message that ran through nearly every session: Africa’s challenges are connected, so African giving has to be connected too. Held from 25 to 27 October under the theme Bridge the Divide; Reimagine the Future , the conference brought together philanthropists, funders, business leaders, creatives, and technologists to ask how African capital can be mobilized, how partnerships can be strengthened, and how African-led solutions can be backed with more trust and flexibility. Centered on Africa, the program also looked outward, drawing on solutions from across the Global South and asking how African philanthropy can bridge the divide. The conference opened on Sunday evening with a reception at Cape Point Vineyards, where Executive Director Mosun Layode welcomed delegates, members and acknowledged APF Board members, including Chair Gbenga Oyebode , Wale Adeosun , and Nyimpini Mabunda . Former Board Member Phuthi Mahanyele-Dabengwa urged guests to look past the continent’s challenges and toward its potential and to use the days ahead to turn conversations into partnerships. It was an evening of connection before two days of ideas at the Norval Foundation. Reimagining the Future Monday, 26 October, began with a call to build bridges across regions, languages, and funding silos. Mosun Layode and Gbenga Oyebode officially opened and welcomed all delegates to the conference. Dr. Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka , former Vice President of South Africa, spoke of education as a sacred right of every African child and of bringing young people into decision-making. In the first keynote, Gary Lubner, Founder of the This Day Foundation, described giving away 95 percent of his wealth during his lifetime and said it was easier and more joyful than holding it for heirs. Old money thinking, he argued, is a major barrier to giving, and generosity includes time and effort as well as cash. The numbers framed the challenge. Delegates heard that Africa needs about $1.3 trillion in financing each year, while philanthropy contributes $5 billion to $6 billion. The task is to use that small pool to unlock far larger sources, such as pension funds and fixed-income assets, so money reaches businesses that create jobs. In an afternoon keynote moderated by Marlene Ogawa of Synergos, Phuthi Mahanyele-Dabengwa , South Africa CEO of Naspers, and Gareth Ackerman, Non-Executive Director at Pick n Pay, kept things practical: back women entrepreneurs without taking equity, start with your own family and community, use local distributors, and make it easier to travel between African countries. One retraining program they discussed moved 7,200 of 8,000 university graduates into tech jobs. The difference between charity and philanthropy, they said, is helping people help themselves. entertainment.title: AI & Equity: The Big Conversations at Goalkeepers Dakar 2026
entertainment.description: The Goalkeepers 2026 Event in Dakar brought together innovators, global leaders and experts on how AI can be further leveraged by Africans for an equitable future On October 29, 2026, Africans gathered in Dakar, Senegal, to discuss the continent’s relationship with the world’s fastest-growing technology: artificial intelligence (AI). This event was part of the Goalkeepers 2026 series and was themed “Make This Matter: Equitable AI and the Future of African Youth .” It brought together professionals and innovators who focused on how Africa can adopt AI to fill gaps and ensure equitable access across various sectors . Africans are leveraging AI for business, education and more, but as AI continues to develop and expand rapidly, it is crucial for us to use it on a bigger scale, ensuring collective development and an equitable future for all. This makes the Goalkeepers 2026 event in Dakar particularly significant. Nigerian influencer, Saskay, at Goalkeepers Dakar 2026 The event included several activities, including performances from the legendary Youssou N’Dour , a Qui veut changer le monden session where people pitched their ideas, conversations about AI and equity and more. Here are some of the major talking points at the event: AI and Existing Solutions The event was graciously hosted in English and French by Fatou Jupiter Toure , who opened by sharing a powerful African message: “It is not about what you can do. It is about what we can do for each other.” Despite the diverse cultures and beliefs that exist on the continent, Africans have remained held by the belief of “I am because you are.” This is why, despite AI’s fast growth, Africans are coming together to examine how much it concerns them, how it can be properly leveraged and what dangers and challenges lie ahead. Fatou Jupiter Toure hosting the Goalkeepers 2026 event in Dakar Nevertheless, Africans have done a great deal of work with AI. Innovators have used AI tools to provide solutions in their local communities. Vyonne Njeri shared how she got into healthcare and how AI has been greatly helping in the community she serves. In the Goalkeepers 2026 Report , Vyonne said she got into healthcare during a visit to see her uncle, a priest in a small, East Kenyan town called Modogashe. She highlighted that even though AI greatly supports her work, she remains the clinical officer. She explained that “AI is not perfect. It must not take over clinical work. But it can help us share across accessible healthcare. It can help discover what could have been missed early. We still need people to be trained, but AI tools can greatly support us.” Like Vyonne, Mamadou Ly also shared why and how AI can aid learning, especially in local languages. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy on Wednesday, court documents showed, per WFAA. Rice reportedly claimed over $3 million in debts in the filing, which came in the Northern District of Texas bankruptcy court. A majority of those listed debts, per ESPN , were tied to "varying plaintiffs suing him in civil litigation that have either been settled or are awaiting trial." Here's what's known about Rice filing for bankruptcy. MORE: NFL trade deadline predictions, projected landing spots Chiefs WR Rashee Rice files for bankruptcy According to WFAA, Rice filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy on Nov. 4, court documents showed, listing his estimated assets to be worth "between $500,000 and $1 million," and his estimated liabilities between "$1 million to $10 million." Rice listed various assets in the filing, including his Super Bowl 53 ring, a Mercedes-Benz, and NFL apparel, per WFAA. ESPN also reported that federal court records showed Rice claimed "more than $3.45 million in debts" in the filing, including more than $2.1 million of which is tied to civil lawsuits that have either been settled or are awaiting trial. The Chiefs wide receiver has been involved in multiple lawsuits tied to his role in a high-speed car crash in Dallas in 2024, along with an ex-girlfriend alleging he repeatedly assaulted her from 2023 to 2025, per ESPN . In July 2025, Rice pleaded guilty to two third-degree felonies in connection with the Dallas car crash incident. He served 30 days in a Dallas County jail in June 2026 after reportedly violating his probation terms after testing positive for THC. According to ESPN, in the bankruptcy filing, Rice claimed to have a total of $677,054 in personal assets, with his largest creditor owed $979,837 as part of a civil settlement related to the 2024 car crash. Rice is also still disputing potential debts from the civil lawsuits, including "a combined $700,000 in lawsuits filed by 2024 crash victims and $200,000 as part of the alleged assault suit," per ESPN. Mandatory Credit: Daniel Dunn-Imagn Images The New York Knicks haven’t had the start to the season they expected, and the reigning champs may have celebrated too hard during the summer. But head coach Mike Brown isn’t worried about his team’s 3-4 start; rather, he’s “a little excited” about their current struggles. On Monday, the Knicks beat the Brooklyn Nets, defeating their neighbors across the bridge 103-90. The team has been off to a slow start, losing its first three games of the season and beginning its rivalry with the Philadelphia 76ers 0-2. The Nets looked competitive early, trailing just 51-44 at halftime, and they took a 79-75 lead into the fourth quarter after a 35-point third. But the defending champs rallied in the fourth quarter, as they are known to do, outscoring Brooklyn 28-11 to seal the deal. The next day, Brown was asked by a reporter, “Are you happy with the starts? Do you think the starts need to get better?” in reference to the team’s energy out of the gate. “Everything can get better,” Brown answered, via SNY Knicks on X . “Am I happy with it? I’m not pissed about the starts or upset about the starts. I’m actually — there’s a part of me… I’m a little excited that we’re struggling a little bit. Because I want to see if we, right now, can figure it out — not figure it out in 10 games and take off and win the last 72, cause that ain’t happening; we’re still going to go through our lulls. But when you go through the off-season that we just went through, where everybody celebrates you the way this lovely city did, and the fans of the New York Knicks did, you want to be shaken and brought back to earth right away when the season starts, because that grounds you; everybody, starting with me on down, obviously, is human, and sometimes you can get a little full of yourself. “So if you hit some challenges or some adversity early on, it helps you refocus a little bit quicker, which can help you get on track the right way sooner. Because right now we could be winning games, but it could be false reality. I said it before: new season, new challenges. Right now, because we’re not playing our best basketball, we’re seeing some of the challenges that we need to work on, and we’re either going to work on them and embrace them, or we’re going to fold, and I don’t think this team has any folding in them, so I’m okay with this.” Finals MVP Jalen Brunson has shown glimpses of last season but hasn’t fully fallen into his normal role just yet either. When asked about his early-season drop in shooting numbers , he chalked it up to just “missing shots” he would “normally make.” Brunson was shooting 39.3% from the field through the first seven games of the 2026-27 season, a major drop-off from his career average of 48.3%. sports.description: Pittsburgh Steelers outside linebacker T.J. Watt in a game against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sept. 27, 2026. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now Two players on the Pittsburgh Steelers could earn some hardware this season. The Pittsburgh Steelers have several players who are playing at a high level and are a big reason why the team currently sits atop the AFC North at 6-2. However, two players in particular have entered the conversation to earn prestigious midseason awards. Steelers outside linebacker T.J. Watt is nominated for NFL Defensive Player of the Year, while rookie wide receiver Germie Bernard is nominated for NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year, per Teresa Varley of Steelers.com . Both players have put together strong cases through the first eight weeks of the 2026 season. Watt has already recorded a league-high 7.5 sacks, 19 tackles, one forced fumble, one fumble recovery, three passes defensed, one interception and one touchdown. Meanwhile, Bernard, the Steelers second-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, has quickly emerged with 32 catches for 284 yards and one touchdown. sports.title: Ducks land in CFP rankings despite rocky season
sports.description: Oregon football’s season hasn’t worked out the way it expected. But the Ducks (5-3, 3-2 Big Ten) were ranked in the first College Football Playoff rankings. Oregon came in at No. 23 in the initial rankings, revealed live on ESPN on Tuesday. Dan Lanning’s team is on the outside looking in at the 12-team playoff, one season before a 24-team playoff is set to likely go into effect. The No. 23 Ducks are coming off a confidence-boosting win over Northwestern, heading on the road to face No. 12 Ohio State (6-2, 4-1) this Saturday. That matchup originally included the preseason Nos. 1 and 2 teams in the AP poll. But in this chaotic college football season, the Buckeyes are reeling after a road loss to No. 20 USC. Other Big Ten teams in this week’s CFP rankings include No. 19 Iowa, No. 8 UCLA and No. 4 Indiana. sports.title: Dodgers Have 2 Intriguing Trade Targets as Marlins Make Infielders Available
sports.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers’ biggest position of need is second base if they want to upgrade offensively on what they have. Tommy Edman is one option at second, along with infield prospect Alex Freeland and possibly even Hyeseong Kim. If the Dodgers want another option, someone who had an impressive 2026 season or a better track record than either Kim or Freeland, the Miami Marlins have a pair of infielders who are reportedly available. Aug 16, 2026; Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; Miami Marlins shortstop Otto Lopez (6) high fives second baseman Xavier Edwards (9) after the victory over the Cincinnati Reds at Great American Ball Park. Mandatory Credit: Katie Stratman-Imagn Images Otto Lopez, shortstop, and Xavier Edwards, second baseman, are two players who, according to Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald , may be traded for “a lot” in exchange. Both Lopez and Edwards have three years of arbitration control, so they are under control until 2030. The Marlins don’t need either of them urgently, but it is an opportunity for at least the Dodgers to explore . Here is what the pair offers: Xavier Edwards Edwards is a multi-positional defender who can play second base and shortstop. His defense declined in 2026 after being above average. Still, he is a walking specialist, with an 11.4% walk rate; he avoids strikeouts (13.9%) and puts the ball in play, but doesn’t hit it hard. More importantly, he’s fast and ranks as an elite base-runner, with at least 21 SBs over the last three years. The Dodgers need speed, and Edwards’s .360 OBP means his speed shows up on the bases. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Dodgers Nation (@dodgersnation) Otto Lopez Lopez is likely the more expensive player, given how amazing his 2026 was. He put up a 5.9 fWAR season, with an above-average hitting season. Lopez slashed .305/.349/.437 with just 11 home runs, but drove in 94 runs, stole 34 bases, and drove in 71 runs. Sep 23, 2025; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Miami Marlins shortstop Xavier Edwards (9) and second base Otto Lopez (6) celebrate win against the Philadelphia Phillies at Citizens Bank Park. Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images It was far and away his best offensive year, since he struggled to get much going before. He is strictly a contact specialist who is a master at putting the ball in play, even if it means a weak walk rate of 5.8%. However, he also plays elite defense, with three straight years as one of the league’s best infielders. Lopez can slot in at either second base or shortstop, and he plays them at a high level. Who should the Dodgers target? Out of the pair, Edwards makes the most sense, since he is likely to cost a bit less and has a more stable track record. Lopez has only one year of hitting at the level he produced in 2026, and for what the Marlins may ask, he may need another season of similar production to warrant that many prospects.

(Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) Getty The New England Patriots‘ six-time Super Bowl-winning head coach Bill Belichick is getting another opportunity to enter the Pro Football Hall of Fame following one of the most controversial snubs in recent memory. Belichick was named one of five remaining coaching candidates for the Hall of Fame’s Class of 2027 on Thursday, Nov. 5, putting him back in contention after he failed to earn induction earlier this year. The 74-year-old joins Tom Coughlin, Mike Holmgren, Dan Reeves and Mike Shanahan in the latest round of consideration, according to Rob Maaddi of the Associated Press. However, Belichick still faces a significant hurdle before officially securing a place in Canton. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) The Hall of Fame’s coaching subcommittee narrowed an initial group of 14 nominees to five, with only one advancing to the final selection process. Belichick finds himself in known territory after reaching the final ballot for the Class of 2026, only to fall short of the votes necessary for induction. ESPN’s Don Van Natta Jr. and Seth Wickersham reported Jan. 27 that Belichick failed to receive the required 40 votes from the 50-member committee, leaving the eight-time Super Bowl champion without a gold jacket. The decision sparked widespread criticism, including from legendary Patriots quarterback Tom Brady , who won six championships alongside Belichick. sports.title: Surprise Team Joins Jonathan Taylor Trade Buzz As Colts Decision Looms
sports.description: LONDON, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 04: Jonathan Taylor of the Indianapolis Colts celebrates after the NFL match between Indianapolis Colts and Washington Commanders as part of the London NFL Series 2026 at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on October 04, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Alex Pantling/Getty Images) Getty The NFL trade deadline is rapidly approaching as November 10 will be here before we know it. The Indianapolis Colts have a lot of decisions to make with regard to which players they want to trade and which ones they want to keep. Running back Jonathan Taylor will be the toughest choice of all and a surprise team has now entered the trade buzz conversation as Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk speculated the San Francisco 49ers might have interest in Taylor. This would be a jarring and shocking move for a number of reasons. First off, the 49ers already have a star running back in Christian McCaffrey. Sure, he may not have the burst that he did five years ago but he is still one of the best dual-threats in the game and can be an absolute nightmare for opposing defenses with his ability to both run the ball and serve as a pass-catcher. So far this season McCaffrey has 84 rushes for 389 yards and eight touchdowns. He also has 34 receptions for 251 yards. While McCaffrey led the NFL in touches last season, San Francisco has done a much better job managing his workload this season. Rookie Kaelon Black has taken on a pretty significant role as the No. 2 back and has come in to spell McCaffrey quite a bit although Black did have a costly fumble in San Francisco’s last game against the Atlanta Falcons when McCaffrey was out for a decent chunk of the game due to a hamstring injury. That hamstring issue is apparently still lingering even after San Francisco’s bye week which is a bit worrisome and perhaps if the 49ers are worried about how available McCaffrey will be the rest of the season then a Taylor trade might end up making more sense. 49ers acquiring Jonathan Taylor would make their offense very scary Acquiring Taylor would give San Francisco yet another weapon to an offense that is pretty dangerous when everyone is healthy. While the team is dealing with lots of injuries right now, imagine a fully healthy offense with McCaffrey, Taylor, George Kittle, Mike Evans, and Deebo Samuel. That would be a fearsome group and having Taylor could allow the Niners to use McCaffrey as more of a slot receiver which they already do at times. Even if a trade for Taylor feels a little far-fetched, the Colts and 49ers could potentially do business on some other players. San Francisco is still in the market for a receiver after their Jauan Jennings deal failed to materialize so maybe the Colts could send Joshua Downs or even Keenan Allen to San Francisco . The Niners are not the likeliest destination for Taylor but with the trade deadline almost here expect some of the trade ideas out there to get even wackier. technology.title: The White House is apparently a popular residential proxy exit spot
technology.description: Whether through malware or other means, devices associated with the White House network appear to be serving as residential proxy exit nodes, potentially posing security risks to one of the world's most sensitive networks. News of the security snafu comes from security firm Layer3 Intel, which reported this week that it discovered the likely illicit activity thanks to its recently launched Residential Proxy Observatory . According to Layer3 founder Sergiy Usatyuk, the White House residential proxy activity might have gone unnoticed if not for the new tool. “The observatory is just a public interface to explore the data we've been collecting for the past year,” Usatyuk told The Register in an email. For those unfamiliar with residential proxies, they're like any old proxy network that obfuscates the location of a user, except in this case their exit nodes use IP addresses associated with residential internet connections, as opposed to datacenters. While many are legitimate, others are exploited by threat actors and used in the commission of cybercrimes, as the FBI warned earlier this year. The FBI bulletin, put out in March, warns users to protect their systems against hijacking via malware, illicit SDK partnerships, VPNs with hidden service terms that repurpose user computers as exit nodes, and other threats used to turn victims into nodes without their consent. Residential proxies are commonly used by threat actors to conceal command-and-control (C2) infrastructure, conduct phishing attacks, send spam, disguise malicious traffic, and the like, the FBI explained. According to Layer3, its data shows 28 distinct residential proxy services exiting into the White House network nearly every day between October 5 and November 3, with 236 separate exits in that period. Other residential proxy detection services logged the same information, Layer3 said. Most of the activity was happening in the evening, White House time, between 5 pm and midnight. That, Layer3 said, suggests someone at the White House - not a guest - has an infected device that’s serving as an exit, likely via an infected proxy SDK. If correct, that’s a problem. “Past research has shown that poorly secured proxy SDKs can allow internal network access and lateral movement,” Layer3 explained. “If an SDK on this network has the same kind of flaw, anyone buying proxy access could use it to reach internal systems.” In other words, this is a serious security risk, and one Usatyuk tells us could have been a problem for a while. “Our data retention period goes back to July 10,” the Layer3 founder explained. “Given that there was continuous activity for a matter of months and other res proxy detection services independently verified the data, it's likely that White House IPs have been used by res proxy networks for all sorts of activity for some time now.” Usatyuk said his firm’s data isn’t detailed enough to know how many machines are being used as exit nodes inside the White House network.
